item.title: An Alaska storm scattered artifacts. Archaeologists are racing to save what's left
item.description: Last year, remnants of a typhoon damaged homes, infrastructure and an archaeological dig site. Now, archaeologists are trying to get as many objects out as possible before the next storm.
item.content:encoded:

item.title: Alaska's salmon-feasting bears face off in biggest Fat Bear Week ever
item.description: This year's single-elimination tournament will see 16 competitors face off, compared to 12 in past years. Officials report more cubs in Katmai National Park than they've seen in recent memory.

item.title: Could trees developed with gene-editing technology protect Florida's citrus industry?
item.description: A bacterial infection is wiping out Florida's citrus trees. Growers hope a rootstock developed with gene-editing technology could keep the disease at bay.
item.content:encoded:

item.title: Here's why an Arizona medical examiner is working to track heat-related deaths
item.description: No one across the U.S. is consistently tracking climate-fueled deaths. One medical examiner has a new protocol on heat-deaths.

item.title: New SpaceX site in Louisiana concerns some residents
item.description: Residents in Louisiana near SpaceX's next launch site are concerned about the project's impact on the environment and say they were kept in dark about the deal.

item.title: Tiny krill are turning up in deep-sea hydrothermal vents. Scientists want to know why
item.description: Antarctic krill serve as a crucial food source for penguins, seals, and whales. They recycle nutrients used by algae. Now researchers say they've found krill in a surprising place: hydrothermal vents.

item.title: EPA rolls back Biden-era rules for power plants that limit greenhouse gas emissions
item.description: The EPA announced Monday its repealing limits on greenhouse gas emissions that come from power plants.
item.content:encoded: The EPA announced Monday its repealing limits on greenhouse gas emissions that come from power plants.

item.title: Trump's EPA repeals pollution limits on fossil fuel power plants
item.description: The Trump administration is eliminating limits on climate-warming pollution from the nation's fossil fuel power plants. Environmental groups say this will impact the climate and public health.

item.title: This summer was hot. August shattered global heat records
item.description: Scientists say that August was the hottest month ever recorded globally. In the U.S., summer temperatures also shattered heat records.

item.title: Scientists say August was Earth's hottest month they've measured
item.description: The European climate service Copernicus said the Earth just sweltered through its hottest month on record in August. Scientists said the heat surge is mostly due to human-caused climate change.
